facts.label: Strongest contrary evidence and what cannot proceed
facts.text: The strongest limit on readiness is that the executed financing documents are absent while the credit-relevant terms (covenant tests, guarantor group, note issuer, security) sit in them. The filings summarise a maintenance test that applies only when revolver usage passes a threshold ((10-Q_2026-09-30_apg-20260930.htm.jsonl page:60: "is greater than 30% of the total revolving credit commitments thereunder subject to a right of cure")), report the ratio as (10-Q_2026-09-30_apg-20260930.htm.jsonl page:60: "Our first lien net leverage ratio as of September 30, 2026 was 1.6:1.0") (rounded to one decimal) and defer the covenant EBITDA definition to filings that do not contain it ((EX-99.1_2026-10-29_apg-20260930xexx991.htm.jsonl page:7: "for the covenant EBITDA definition")). Consequence: CP-1 can state the reported ratio, the threshold and the printed revolver, letter-of-credit and commitment amounts, but cannot recompute covenant leverage or confirm whether the 30% usage trigger was met under the credit agreement's definitions. Source risk mechanism: a springing covenant whose trigger and EBITDA definition are outside the pack leaves covenant headroom a filing-summary claim, not a verified figure.

facts.label: Financial base view
facts.text: The financial base is sound on reported earnings and weaker on balance sheet capacity. Revenue and adjusted EBITDA grew through FY2025 and the first nine months of 2026, and free cash flow after capex remained positive, but 2026 acquisitions of 1,356 million (cash, net) and share repurchases of 252 million were funded by a 500 million senior note issue, revolver borrowing and a 539 million fall in cash, moving net debt up by 1,364 million in nine months. On the issuer's adjusted EBITDA, last-twelve-months total leverage is 3.02x and net leverage 2.71x, against 2.67x and 1.79x at FY2025; liquidity of 1,032 million at September 30, 2026 compares with 1,657 million at FY2025. Two further points shape the view: the last-twelve-months EBITDA includes acquired businesses only from their closing dates while their purchase price is fully in debt, so leverage is overstated against a pro forma run-rate, and interest cost is understated by cash paid, because the 500 million 5.750% notes issued on May 14, 2026 and the revolver draw have only partly reached the cash interest line. Debt matures in 2029 (two note series), 2031 (revolver), 2033 (term loan) and 2034, so there is no near-term wall, but the 335 million revolver balance appears to be classified as short-term debt and the credit agreement's covenant definitions are not supplied. All adjusted measures are management-defined; reported (unadjusted) EBITDA gives 3.61x total and 3.23x net leverage on the same last-twelve-months basis, and the add-backs are material (systems and business enablement alone is 82 million for nine months 2026).

facts.label: Covenant, liquidity and refinancing position
facts.text: The only financial maintenance covenant described is a springing first lien net leverage test on the revolver, with a limit of 3.75 to 1.00 for each fiscal quarter. The Q3 report states the limit and the trigger and reports the ratio ((10-Q_2026-09-30_apg-20260930.htm.jsonl page:60: "Our first lien net leverage ratio as of September 30, 2026 was 1.6:1.0")); the ratio was (10-Q_2026-06-30_apg-20260630.htm.jsonl page:59: "Our first lien net leverage ratio as of June 30, 2026 was 1.3:1.0") at June 30, 2026 and (10-K_2025-12-31_apg-20251231.htm.jsonl page:73: "Our first lien net leverage ratio as of December 31, 2025 was 1.1:1.0") at year-end. The trigger is (10-Q_2026-09-30_apg-20260930.htm.jsonl page:60: "is greater than 30% of the total revolving credit commitments thereunder subject to a right of cure") measured on revolving loans and letter of credit obligations excluding undrawn letters of credit up to 60. On the filing wording, usage at September 30, 2026 was 335 drawn of 1,000 commitments, which is 33.5% and above the trigger; at June 30, 2026 it was 280 of 1,000 (28.0%), below it; and at October 29, 2026 it was 435 of 1,000 (43.5%). The test therefore applied at the latest quarter-end on the filing's own description, with reported headroom of 2.15x on rounded figures (3.75 less 1.6). facts.label: Covenant, liquidity and refinancing position
facts.text: Liquidity is cash plus undrawn revolver: 373 + 659 = 1,032 at September 30, 2026 ((10-Q_2026-09-30_apg-20260930.htm.jsonl page:56: "$1,032 million of total liquidity")), down from 912 + 745 = 1,657 at December 31, 2025 and 499 + 494 = 993 at December 31, 2024. No committed facility expires within twelve months: the revolver matures in 2031 and the term loan in 2033 after the Ninth Amendment; the 2029 notes are the first bond maturities. Hedging: (10-Q_2026-09-30_apg-20260930.htm.jsonl page:24: "the 2026 Interest Rate Swap with $720 of notional value, exchanging one-month SOFR for a fixed rate of 3.59% per annum") and a second swap of 400 notional; (10-Q_2026-09-30_apg-20260930.htm.jsonl page:25: "The remaining $1,027 of the term loan balance will bear interest based on one-month SOFR plus 175 basis points"); the 720 forward-starting swap matures in January 2029 ((10-Q_2026-09-30_apg-20260930.htm.jsonl page:25: "commencing in October 2026 and maturing in January 2029")), before the term loan maturity in 2033, so floating exposure on the term loan returns thereafter. Fixed coupons on the three note series total about 56 a year (Calculations). The issuer-reported fair values at September 30, 2026 were 318 for the 4.125% notes, 263 for the 4.750% notes and 473 for the 5.750% notes (carrying values 337, 277 and 500), i.e. all three below carrying value; fair values are issuer estimates from discounting at available rates (Level 2), not traded prices.

facts.label: Business and transaction view
facts.text: APi Group Corporation is a US-listed holding company whose subsidiaries deliver fire and life safety, security, elevator and escalator, and specialty contracting, fabrication and infrastructure services, reported as two segments, Safety Services and Specialty Services. Safety Services, which is mostly contracted inspection, service and monitoring plus installation, carried FY2025 revenue of 5,456, with Specialty Services at 2,460, and about two thirds of revenue is United States based. The creditor-relevant strengths are documented diversification (no customer above 5% of 2025 net revenues), statutory and insurance-driven inspection demand described by management, a cost base the company describes as largely variable, and capital spending that management puts below 1.5% of net revenues. facts.label: Credit translations
facts.text: 1. Revenue durability (Analyst Interpretation). Evidence: contracted inspection and service demand described as statutory and insurance-driven ((10-K_2025-12-31_apg-20251231.htm.jsonl page:10: "Inspections are often required by legislation or insurance mandates, providing a strong recurring revenue stream")), no customer above 5%, remaining performance obligations of 4,863. Risk mechanic: demand for inspection and service work is less discretionary, supporting steady cash flow, but project and fixed-price work in both segments exposes margin to cost overruns and mix, and contract terms are mostly under six months. Credit implication: supports debt service capacity in a downturn better than a pure contractor would, but durability cannot be sized without the recurring share, which is not disclosed. Counter-evidence: Q3 2026 gross margin fell year on year (CP-1) and the audit-matter on fixed-price estimates. 2. Acquisition-driven leverage (Analyst Interpretation). Evidence: 1,356 of acquisition spend in nine months 2026 (CP-1) and last-twelve-months total debt over adjusted EBITDA of 3.02x and net 2.71x (CP-1, derived). Risk mechanic: purchase prices are fully in debt and cash while acquired EBITDA enters the trailing figure only from closing dates, so reported leverage overstates run-rate leverage but also depends on unproven integration. Credit implication: deleveraging depends on organic growth and integration rather than debt paydown, because buybacks continue; refinancing risk is limited by 2029 and later maturities. Counter-evidence: the 2025 acquisition consideration totals differ across filings (conflict 1), showing purchase accounting can move. 3. Capital allocation (Analyst Interpretation). Evidence: repurchases of 252 in nine months 2026 and about 143 after quarter-end alongside a further 100 revolver draw. Risk mechanic: shareholder returns compete with debt reduction while revolver usage sits above the 30% springing-covenant trigger (CP-1). Credit implication: management tolerates higher leverage for growth and returns; the documents showing what limits exist are not supplied, so monitoring posture should stay watchful. 4. Sponsor alignment (Insufficient Information). Beneficial ownership percentages and control rights are not disclosed in the pack; related-party fees and Series A share dividends are small and disclosed. Missing datapoint: ownership concentration, which matters for willingness to support the credit or extract value.

facts.label: Credit view
facts.text: APi Group Corp is a sound, cash-generative services business whose credit profile weakened in 2026 because acquisitions and buybacks were funded with debt. Its strongest support is diversified, regulation-driven demand, with no customer above 5% of FY2025 net revenues, adjusted EBITDA of USD 896 million for nine months 2026, and debt maturities that start in 2029 apart from small short-term loans. The weakest point is balance sheet capacity: last-twelve-months total debt over adjusted EBITDA is 3.02x (net 2.71x) against 2.67x (1.79x) at FY2025, liquidity is USD 1,032 million, and revolver usage is above the springing-covenant trigger. Whether the rise proves temporary depends on integrating the USD 1,197 million of named 2026 acquisitions and on restraint in buybacks; unverified covenant definitions limit confidence.

The weakest point is balance sheet capacity: last-twelve-months total debt over adjusted EBITDA is 3.02x (net 2.71x) against 2.67x (1.79x) at FY2025, liquidity is USD 1,032 million, and revolver usage is above the springing-covenant trigger. facts.label: Key findings
facts.text: First, leverage stepped up sharply in nine months 2026 (Analyst Interpretation on CP-1 figures). Total debt obligations rose to USD 3,601 million from USD 2,776 million at FY2025 and cash fell to USD 373 million from USD 912 million, so net debt rose by USD 1,364 million [CP-1, leverage and Calculations]. The mechanism is that acquisition spend of USD 1,356 million (net of cash acquired; named deals CertaSite, Onyx-Fire and WTech cost USD 1,197 million combined) and buybacks of USD 252 million exceeded free cash flow of USD 317 million, and the acquired EBITDA enters the trailing figure only from closing dates, so reported leverage overstates run-rate leverage while also resting on unproven integration [CP-1; CP-1A, transaction summary]. The implication is a lower cushion against a margin or volume shock until earnings catch up, with last-twelve-months cash interest cover of 9.23x flattering the position because the USD 500 million 5.750% notes issued in May 2026 and the revolver draw have only partly reached cash interest; Q3 2026 interest expense, net, was USD 45 million against USD 34 million a year earlier, and an annualised Q3 figure gives about 6.62x (indicative, CP-1) (Analyst Interpretation).

facts.label: Key findings
facts.text: Second, liquidity is adequate but thinner (Documentary Fact on CP-1 figures). Liquidity was USD 1,032 million at September 30, 2026 (USD 373 million cash and USD 659 million undrawn revolver), against USD 1,657 million at FY2025, and revolver availability was USD 559 million at October 29, 2026 after a further USD 100 million draw, a subsequent event. The revolver matures in 2031 and the term loan in 2033 after the Ninth Amendment, and the notes mature in 2029 and 2034, so there is no near-term wall; the implication is that debt service and refinancing risk are manageable, but the revolver is now the funding buffer for seasonal cash flow, with operating cash flow back-end loaded.

facts.label: Key findings
facts.text: Third, the only maintenance covenant is a springing first lien net leverage test that applies at the latest quarter-end (Documentary Fact for the reported ratio, Analyst Interpretation for the trigger). Revolver usage of 33.5% exceeded the 30% trigger at September 30, 2026, and the reported ratio of 1.6:1.0 compares with a 3.75 to 1.00 limit, 2.15x of headroom on rounded figures [CP-1, covenant position]. The credit agreement is not supplied, so the covenant EBITDA definition is unverified; CP-1's indicative implied covenant EBITDA of about USD 1,318 million against derived last-twelve-months adjusted EBITDA of USD 1,191 million depends on pro forma adjustments the issuer describes but the pack does not quantify. facts.label: Strengths and weaknesses
facts.text: Strengths. (1) Customer diversification and regulation-driven demand: no customer above 5% of FY2025 net revenues, statutory and insurance-driven inspection demand per management (Documentary Fact for the concentration, Management Language for the demand characterisation) [CP-1A, company profile]; the mechanism is lower single-name revenue risk and less discretionary service demand, implying steadier cash flow than a pure project contractor. (2) Earnings momentum: adjusted EBITDA of USD 896 million for nine months 2026 against USD 746 million, with revenue up in both segments (Documentary Fact) [CP-1]; implying capacity to absorb the acquisition debt if growth persists. (3) Debt structure and market access: maturities begin in 2029 with fixed-rate notes, an extended revolver (2031) and term loan (2033), and a USD 500 million note issue completed in May 2026 (Documentary Fact) [CP-1; CP-1A]; implying low refinancing pressure and demonstrated market access. (4) Low capital intensity: free cash flow after capex of USD 317 million in nine months 2026 and capex management puts below 1.5% of net revenues (Documentary Fact for the cash figure, Management Language for the claim) [CP-1; CP-1A]; implying the business converts EBITDA to cash outside working capital swings. (5) Wide reported covenant headroom of 2.15x (Documentary Fact, unverified definitions) [CP-1].

facts.label: Strengths and weaknesses
facts.text: Weaknesses. (1) Higher leverage from debt-funded acquisitions: 3.02x total and 2.71x net on last-twelve-months adjusted EBITDA (Documentary Fact on derived CP-1 figures); the mechanism is purchase prices in debt before acquired earnings fully arrive, implying thinner cushion and dependence on integration. Reported (unadjusted) EBITDA gives 3.61x and 3.23x, and the add-backs are material, so the choice of EBITDA measure matters (CP-1). (2) Capital returns alongside leverage build: USD 252 million of buybacks plus about USD 143 million after quarter-end (Documentary Fact); implying deleveraging relies on earnings growth rather than debt paydown. (3) Springing covenant trigger exceeded and definitions unverified (Documentary Fact for usage, Insufficient Information for the covenant mechanics). (4) Revenue durability unquantified and project exposure: the recurring share is not disclosed, contracts are mostly under six months, fixed-price estimation is a critical audit matter and Q3 2026 gross margin fell (Documentary Fact; Insufficient Information for the recurring share) [CP-1A]; implying margin and cash volatility that cannot be sized. (5) Rising and partly floating interest cost: the term loan floats on SOFR with hedges that end before its 2033 maturity (the forward swap matures in January 2029), and the new notes carry a 5.750% coupon (Documentary Fact) [CP-1]; implying higher interest burden after the swaps roll off. (6) Documentation gaps: no credit agreement, indentures or guarantor list, and unresolved issuer of record for the notes (Insufficient Information) [CP-0; CP-1A].

Question: can the supplied source set support the selected downstream modules (CP-1, CP-1A, CP-2, CP-5), and what remains blocked. This module gives no credit conclusion, legal interpretation or investment opinion, and it performs no analytical calculation. Source sufficiency is distinct from completion of downstream analysis.

The run context (sha256 below) holds the dated run settings only; it is not issuer evidence. It leaves ratings, quotes, deal terms, valuation inputs and research questions blank, sets legal documents to "none" and names no borrower, parent or guarantors. None. CP-0 is the first module in this run and no upstream handoff exists, so none was consumed.
### Coverage method

Each source is a text extraction ("Visible text of ..." per page, retained as page:N chunks). Page chunks are extraction units, not printed page numbers. Retained units: 153 pages (annual report), 53, 65 and 66 pages (Q1, Q2, Q3 quarterly reports), 17, 15 and 15 pages (Q1, Q2, Q3 releases), which is 384 retained units. Readiness rests on full-text search of every retained unit and on direct reading of the units cited below. ## Findings
### Reader summary
| Bottom line | Confidence | Main limitation |

| The seven supplied filings and releases can support a credit snapshot of APi Group Corp as of 2026-11-05, with bounded limitations. Legal documents are not supplied, so covenant and guarantor terms rest on filing summaries. | Medium | No credit agreement, indentures or guarantor list is supplied; covenant EBITDA definition is not in the pack. |

| Debt changed in 2026: a new senior note issue, a larger revolver, extended maturities for the term loan and revolver, and further revolver borrowing after quarter-end. | Debt and maturity analysis must use the latest quarterly report, because the annual report shows superseded terms. | High |

### Readiness view

The effective source set is READY_WITH_LIMITATIONS for all four selected consumers. The filed statements, debt notes, liquidity discussion, segment notes, acquisition notes and subsequent-event notes needed for a credit snapshot are present and located in the latest quarterly report, with the annual report giving the FY2025 base and the releases giving attributed adjusted measures and guidance. No consumer is CONDITIONAL or BLOCKED: no source shows blocked preparation in the run output, no identity boundary is unresolved to the point of preventing the work, and every limitation below is bounded. The recurring limitations to carry forward are the absence of executed legal documents (credit agreement, amendments, indentures), the unenumerated guarantor group, the unresolved issuer-of-record wording for the notes, the covenant EBITDA definition that the sources only refer to, and the text-only extraction. This is a source-sufficiency assertion only (SOURCE_SUFFICIENCY_ONLY; CP_MODEL_INPUT_CONTRACT_NOT_EVALUATED): it does not assert normalized quarters, reconciliation or acceptance of any downstream input.

| CP-1A (business and transaction context) | READY_WITH_LIMITATIONS | Business description, segments, 2026 acquisitions, financing events, related-party and preferred-stock facts | No acquisition agreements, credit agreement or indentures; guarantor group not enumerated; issuer-of-record wording differs between documents |

| CP-2 (fundamental credit synthesis) | READY_WITH_LIMITATIONS | Draws on upstream CP-1 and CP-1A only; the underlying evidence is located as above | Inherits every CP-1 and CP-1A limitation; no ratings or market data supplied |

| CP-5 (evidence trace validation) | READY_WITH_LIMITATIONS | Every cited fact below carries an exact quote and page:N locator in a retained source | Pages are extraction chunks; releases are management claims; no original-HTML fidelity check |
### Source-by-source assessment
#### Annual report, FY2025

Identity and period: (10-K_2025-12-31_apg-20251231.htm.jsonl page:1: "For the fiscal year ended December 31, 2025") with (10-K_2025-12-31_apg-20251231.htm.jsonl page:1: "Commission File Number 001-39275"). Authority: audited filed statements (auditor signature (10-K_2025-12-31_apg-20251231.htm.jsonl page:85: "/s/ KPMG LLP")). Content located: balance sheet ((10-K_2025-12-31_apg-20251231.htm.jsonl page:85: "Cash and cash equivalents $ 912 $ 499")), operations ((10-K_2025-12-31_apg-20251231.htm.jsonl page:86: "Net revenues $ 7,911 $ 7,018 $ 6,928")), cash flows ((10-K_2025-12-31_apg-20251231.htm.jsonl page:88: "Cash paid for interest, net of interest income $ 136 $ 152 $ 150")), debt note ((10-K_2025-12-31_apg-20251231.htm.jsonl page:121: "2021 Term Loan January 3, 2029 $ 2,157 $ 2,157")), maturity table ((10-K_2025-12-31_apg-20251231.htm.jsonl page:123: "2029 2,771")), segment note and a lease note. It is the base for FY2025 and the superseded debt terms; later quarterly reports control any fact they restate.
#### Quarterly reports, Q1, Q2 and Q3 2026

Q3 identity and period: (10-Q_2026-09-30_apg-20260930.htm.jsonl page:1: "For the quarterly period ended September 30, 2026"). Statements present three-month and nine-month columns ((10-Q_2026-09-30_apg-20260930.htm.jsonl page:3: "Net revenues $ 2,554 $ 2,085 $ 6,790 $ 5,794")) and the September 30, 2026 balance sheet against December 31, 2025 ((10-Q_2026-09-30_apg-20260930.htm.jsonl page:2: "Cash and cash equivalents $ 373 $ 912")). The Q1 and Q2 reports give the intermediate quarter-end balance sheets, debt tables and covenant ratios, so discrete quarters and year-to-date amounts are separable by period label. Facility-level debt carrying values are in the Q3 debt note ((10-Q_2026-09-30_apg-20260930.htm.jsonl page:23: "Total debt obligations 3,601 2,776")). Cash-paid interest is in the Q3 cash flow statement ((10-Q_2026-09-30_apg-20260930.htm.jsonl page:5: "Cash paid for interest, net of interest income $ 98 $ 105")). The quarterly reports contain no lease note; operating and finance lease liabilities appear only as balance sheet lines ((10-Q_2026-09-30_apg-20260930.htm.jsonl page:2: "Operating and finance leases 101 98")).
#### Earnings releases, Q1, Q2 and Q3 2026

These are management-attributed supporting sources. The Q3 release states (EX-99.1_2026-10-29_apg-20260930xexx991.htm.jsonl page:1: "Record third quarter adjusted EBITDA of $350 million") and provides the reconciliation ((EX-99.1_2026-10-29_apg-20260930xexx991.htm.jsonl page:11: "Adjusted EBITDA $ 350 $ 281 $ 896 $ 746")), the adjusted free cash flow reconciliation ((EX-99.1_2026-10-29_apg-20260930xexx991.htm.jsonl page:15: "Adjusted free cash flow $ 240 $ 248 $ 468 $ 434")) and guidance ((EX-99.1_2026-10-29_apg-20260930xexx991.htm.jsonl page:3: "Net revenues of $9,200 to $9,250 million")). Adjusted measures are non-GAAP and cannot override the filed statements. The Q1 and Q2 releases are retained as separate sources for the prior-quarter series and prior guidance; none is a duplicate of another, and none supersedes a filing.
### Entity and perimeter

The registrant and reporting entity is APi Group Corporation, with consolidated statements of "APi Group Corporation and subsidiaries" (context name: APi Group Corp; NYSE ticker APG shown on the cover). The borrower of the credit facilities is a subsidiary: (10-Q_2026-09-30_apg-20260930.htm.jsonl page:58: "a Credit Agreement by and among APi Group DE, Inc., our wholly-owned subsidiary, as borrower"), with the parent as guarantor and Citibank N.A. as administrative and collateral agent. The senior notes are described as guaranteed by the parent and "certain of our subsidiaries" ((10-K_2025-12-31_apg-20251231.htm.jsonl page:73: "fully and unconditionally guaranteed on a senior unsecured basis by us and certain of our subsidiaries")). No restricted or unrestricted subsidiary split, guarantor schedule or separate issuer financials is supplied; all supplied financials are consolidated. The 10-K and 10-Q describe a senior secured revolver ("Revolving Credit Facility") and a term loan under one Credit Agreement; the legal security package is not documented in the pack.
### Reporting periods and basis

All amounts are USD millions as printed, on a US GAAP basis; the sources use calendar fiscal quarters. Supplied periods: FY2025 (and FY2024 and FY2023 comparatives in the 10-K), Q1, Q2 and Q3 2026 with the prior-year comparatives, six and nine months 2026, and quarter-end balance sheets at December 31, 2025, March 31, June 30 and September 30, 2026. Geographic revenue is split United States, France and Other ((10-Q_2026-09-30_apg-20260930.htm.jsonl page:12: "France 525 — — 525")). Not supplied as a stand-alone period: Q4 2025, because no fourth-quarter release is in the pack; a last-twelve-months figure is not printed anywhere in the sources (searched for LTM and trailing twelve months). All sources are dated on or before 2026-10-29, within the cutoff; the latest, the Q3 release and report, are dated October 29, 2026. One subsequent event is dated before the cutoff and is carried as such: (10-Q_2026-09-30_apg-20260930.htm.jsonl page:24: "Subsequent to September 30, 2026, the Company borrowed an additional $100 under the Revolving Credit Facility for general corporate purposes").
### Version relationships and changes between sources
These are amendments and updates, kept as separate active sources; the later filing controls a restated fact only where it says so.
| Item | Earlier source | Later source | Note |

| 2021 Term Loan maturity | (10-K_2025-12-31_apg-20251231.htm.jsonl page:121: "2021 Term Loan January 3, 2029 $ 2,157 $ 2,157") | (10-Q_2026-09-30_apg-20260930.htm.jsonl page:22: "2021 Term Loan May 14, 2033 $ 2,147 $ 2,157") | Later report attributes the extension to the Ninth Amendment ((10-Q_2026-09-30_apg-20260930.htm.jsonl page:24: "extended the maturity date of the 2021 Term Loan to May 14, 2033")); the amendment text itself is not supplied |

| Revolver size and maturity | $750 million, maturing May 20, 2030 per the 10-K debt table | (10-Q_2026-09-30_apg-20260930.htm.jsonl page:24: "increased the Revolving Credit Facility by $250, from $750 to $1,000") and maturity May 14, 2031 | Availability after letters of credit moved from $745 million at year-end to $659 million at September 30, 2026 ((10-Q_2026-09-30_apg-20260930.htm.jsonl page:56: "$1,032 million of total liquidity")) |

| Senior notes | Two series at year-end | A third series added in Q2 2026 ((10-Q_2026-09-30_apg-20260930.htm.jsonl page:60: "On May 14, 2026, APi Group DE completed a private offering of $500 million aggregate principal amount of 5.750% Senior Notes due 2034")) | Indenture of May 14, 2026 not supplied |

| Pending acquisitions | (10-Q_2026-03-31_apg-20260331.htm.jsonl page:30: "Wtech will be acquired for approximately €324 in cash") (signed, April 17, 2026) | Closed: (10-Q_2026-09-30_apg-20260930.htm.jsonl page:8: "On July 1, 2026, the Company completed the acquisition of WTech Fire Group") | Purchase accounting is provisional ((10-Q_2026-09-30_apg-20260930.htm.jsonl page:9: "The Company has not finalized its accounting for any of the acquisitions completed during 2026")) |
### Source differences and conflicts, with downstream effect
Each item is logged as found; none is reconciled or resolved here.

1. Letter-of-credit exclusion in the springing covenant. The annual report says (10-K_2025-12-31_apg-20251231.htm.jsonl page:73: "(excluding undrawn letters of credit up to $40 million)"); the Q3 report says (10-Q_2026-09-30_apg-20260930.htm.jsonl page:60: "excluding undrawn letters of credit up to $60 million"). Likely a result of the 2026 amendment, but the amendment is not supplied. Effect: CP-1 must use the Q3 wording for the current test and flag the change.

2. Term loan amortization. The annual report says (10-K_2025-12-31_apg-20251231.htm.jsonl page:72: "we do not owe any quarterly principal amounts for the remainder of the 2021 Term Loan"); the Q3 report says (10-Q_2026-09-30_apg-20260930.htm.jsonl page:59: "Principal payments on the 2021 Term Loan will be made in quarterly installments on the last day of each fiscal quarter"). The reason for the change is not stated in the supplied text. Effect: the debt schedule for CP-1 should follow the Q3 report and note the change as unexplained.

3. Issuer of record for the notes. The MD&A says (10-K_2025-12-31_apg-20251231.htm.jsonl page:73: "On June 22, 2021, APi Group DE completed a private offering of $350 million aggregate principal amount of 4.125% Senior Notes due 2029"), while the exhibit index lists the indenture as (10-K_2025-12-31_apg-20251231.htm.jsonl page:150: "Indenture, dated as of June 22, 2021, by and among APi Group Corporation, the guarantors party thereto and Computershare Trust Company, N.A."). The indentures are not supplied, so the legal issuer, co-issuer and guarantor roles remain unresolved. Effect: CP-1 and CP-1A must describe the notes as issued and guaranteed per the MD&A wording and mark issuer identity as a gap.

4. Share repurchase amount. The Q3 MD&A says (10-Q_2026-09-30_apg-20260930.htm.jsonl page:57: "we repurchased 6,338,563 shares of common stock for approximately $250 million") for the nine months, while the cash flow statement shows (10-Q_2026-09-30_apg-20260930.htm.jsonl page:5: "Repurchases of common stock (252)"). The basis difference (for example settlement timing) is not stated. Effect: minor; use the cash flow amount for cash and the MD&A for share count, with the difference noted.

5. Stale covenant wording. The Q1 report still carries (10-Q_2026-03-31_apg-20260331.htm.jsonl page:47: "(i) 4.00 to 1.00 for each fiscal quarter ending in 2021"), which is boilerplate for periods long past; the current test level in the same sentence is 3.75 to 1.00. Effect: none beyond citing the current level.

6. Location counts differ by date: (10-K_2025-12-31_apg-20251231.htm.jsonl page:8: "over 500 locations worldwide") in the annual report and (EX-99.1_2026-10-29_apg-20260930xexx991.htm.jsonl page:4: "With more than 600 locations in over 20 countries") in the Q3 release, the latter management-attributed and after 2026 acquisitions. Effect: CP-1A should cite each with its date.

Extraction observation (not an issuer conflict): the Q3 report's note heading splits across extraction units ((10-Q_2026-09-30_apg-20260930.htm.jsonl page:28: "NOTE 13.") ends one unit and (10-Q_2026-09-30_apg-20260930.htm.jsonl page:29: "RELATED-PARTY TRANSACTIONS The Company incurred advisory fees") begins the next). Locators should name both units where a note spans them.
### Strongest contrary evidence and what cannot proceed

The strongest limit on readiness is that the executed financing documents are absent while the credit-relevant terms (covenant tests, guarantor group, note issuer, security) sit in them. The filings summarise a maintenance test that applies only when revolver usage passes a threshold ((10-Q_2026-09-30_apg-20260930.htm.jsonl page:60: "is greater than 30% of the total revolving credit commitments thereunder subject to a right of cure")), report the ratio as (10-Q_2026-09-30_apg-20260930.htm.jsonl page:60: "Our first lien net leverage ratio as of September 30, 2026 was 1.6:1.0") (rounded to one decimal) and defer the covenant EBITDA definition to filings that do not contain it ((EX-99.1_2026-10-29_apg-20260930xexx991.htm.jsonl page:7: "for the covenant EBITDA definition")). Consequence: CP-1 can state the reported ratio, the threshold and the printed revolver, letter-of-credit and commitment amounts, but cannot recompute covenant leverage or confirm whether the 30% usage trigger was met under the credit agreement's definitions. Source risk mechanism: a springing covenant whose trigger and EBITDA definition are outside the pack leaves covenant headroom a filing-summary claim, not a verified figure.

Other things that cannot proceed on this source set: rating-agency views (only an incidental mention appears, (10-K_2025-12-31_apg-20251231.htm.jsonl page:119: "ratings have remained stable at BB and Ba2 in 2025"), inside a lease discount-rate discussion), market-based valuation (context market inputs blank), peer comparison, and guarantor or structural-subordination analysis by legal entity.
### Context facts located for CP-1A

For the business and transaction consumer: the 2026 acquisitions are located with consideration ((10-Q_2026-09-30_apg-20260930.htm.jsonl page:8: "On February 2, 2026, the Company completed the acquisition of CertaSite, LLC"); (10-Q_2026-09-30_apg-20260930.htm.jsonl page:8: "On June 8, 2026, the Company completed the acquisition of Onyx-Fire Protection Services, Inc."); WTech above), with Onyx-Fire acquired (10-Q_2026-03-31_apg-20260331.htm.jsonl page:30: "from funds managed by Blackstone Tactical Opportunities") per the Q1 report. Ownership and governance facts located: (10-Q_2026-09-30_apg-20260930.htm.jsonl page:29: "payable to Mariposa Capital, LLC") and Series A Preferred Stock that (10-Q_2026-09-30_apg-20260930.htm.jsonl page:29: "will be convertible into 6,000,000 shares of common stock upon conversion on the last day of 2026"), a future date stated as a contract term. Share repurchases after quarter-end are located ((10-Q_2026-09-30_apg-20260930.htm.jsonl page:37: "Subsequent to September 30, 2026, the Company repurchased 3,604,478 shares of common stock for approximately $143 under the 2025 SRP")). Contracted revenue visibility is located as remaining performance obligations ((10-K_2025-12-31_apg-20251231.htm.jsonl page:107: "was $3,605") at year-end, (10-Q_2026-09-30_apg-20260930.htm.jsonl page:12: "was $4,863") at September 30, 2026); these are accounting measures for in-process contracts and are not the same as backlog.
## Calculations

No analytical calculation was performed. CP-0 does not normalize, reconcile or derive figures. Two extraction-fidelity tie-outs only, each comparing printed components with a printed total in the same table:
| Check | Inputs (all printed) | Result |
| Q3 debt table foots | 2,147 + 335 + 337 + 277 + 500 + 5 (Q3 debt note, September 30, 2026) | 3,601, equals the printed total debt obligations |
| Q3 debt carried on the balance sheet | 3,601 less unamortized deferred financing costs 27 (Q3 debt note) | 3,574, equals current debt 361 plus long-term debt 3,213 on the balance sheet |

Both tie-outs confirm the extraction matches the filing arithmetic; they do not establish fidelity to the original HTML. | Bottom line | Confidence | Main limitation |

| Total debt obligations rose from 2,776 million at FY2025 to 3,601 million at September 30, 2026; cash fell from 912 million to 373 million. | Net debt over adjusted EBITDA rose to 2.71x from 1.79x, so the balance sheet carries much less cushion than at FY2025. | High |

| Adjusted EBITDA grew to 896 million for nine months 2026 from 746 million, and cash interest cover is 9.23x on a last-twelve-months basis. | Earnings growth partly offsets the higher debt, but the cash interest figure may not yet reflect the full cost of the new 5.750% notes. | Medium |

| Nine-month operating cash flow was 393 million against 1,356 million of acquisition spend and 252 million of buybacks. | Shareholder returns and acquisitions outran internally generated cash, so the funding gap came from borrowing and the cash balance. | High |

| The springing first lien test was reported at 1.6:1.0 against a limit of 3.75 to 1.00, and revolver usage of 33.5% exceeded the 30% trigger. | Reported headroom is wide, but the test applies now and its EBITDA definition cannot be checked. | Medium |
### Financial base view

The financial base is sound on reported earnings and weaker on balance sheet capacity. Revenue and adjusted EBITDA grew through FY2025 and the first nine months of 2026, and free cash flow after capex remained positive, but 2026 acquisitions of 1,356 million (cash, net) and share repurchases of 252 million were funded by a 500 million senior note issue, revolver borrowing and a 539 million fall in cash, moving net debt up by 1,364 million in nine months. On the issuer's adjusted EBITDA, last-twelve-months total leverage is 3.02x and net leverage 2.71x, against 2.67x and 1.79x at FY2025; liquidity of 1,032 million at September 30, 2026 compares with 1,657 million at FY2025. Two further points shape the view: the last-twelve-months EBITDA includes acquired businesses only from their closing dates while their purchase price is fully in debt, so leverage is overstated against a pro forma run-rate, and interest cost is understated by cash paid, because the 500 million 5.750% notes issued on May 14, 2026 and the revolver draw have only partly reached the cash interest line. Debt matures in 2029 (two note series), 2031 (revolver), 2033 (term loan) and 2034, so there is no near-term wall, but the 335 million revolver balance appears to be classified as short-term debt and the credit agreement's covenant definitions are not supplied. All adjusted measures are management-defined; reported (unadjusted) EBITDA gives 3.61x total and 3.23x net leverage on the same last-twelve-months basis, and the add-backs are material (systems and business enablement alone is 82 million for nine months 2026).

### Covenant, liquidity and refinancing position

The only financial maintenance covenant described is a springing first lien net leverage test on the revolver, with a limit of 3.75 to 1.00 for each fiscal quarter. The Q3 report states the limit and the trigger and reports the ratio ((10-Q_2026-09-30_apg-20260930.htm.jsonl page:60: "Our first lien net leverage ratio as of September 30, 2026 was 1.6:1.0")); the ratio was (10-Q_2026-06-30_apg-20260630.htm.jsonl page:59: "Our first lien net leverage ratio as of June 30, 2026 was 1.3:1.0") at June 30, 2026 and (10-K_2025-12-31_apg-20251231.htm.jsonl page:73: "Our first lien net leverage ratio as of December 31, 2025 was 1.1:1.0") at year-end. The trigger is (10-Q_2026-09-30_apg-20260930.htm.jsonl page:60: "is greater than 30% of the total revolving credit commitments thereunder subject to a right of cure") measured on revolving loans and letter of credit obligations excluding undrawn letters of credit up to 60. On the filing wording, usage at September 30, 2026 was 335 drawn of 1,000 commitments, which is 33.5% and above the trigger; at June 30, 2026 it was 280 of 1,000 (28.0%), below it; and at October 29, 2026 it was 435 of 1,000 (43.5%). The test therefore applied at the latest quarter-end on the filing's own description, with reported headroom of 2.15x on rounded figures (3.75 less 1.6). This relies on summarised wording; the credit agreement and its definitions are not supplied, so whether the trigger and ratio are computed exactly this way is a stated limitation. An indicative reading of the covenant EBITDA: first lien debt (term loan 2,147 plus revolver 335, less cash 373, giving 2,109) over the reported 1.6x implies an EBITDA of about 1,318 (range 1,278 to 1,361 for ratio rounding), against derived LTM adjusted EBITDA of 1,191; the gap of about 127 is consistent with the pro forma and cost-savings adjustments the release mentions ((EX-99.1_2026-10-29_apg-20260930xexx991.htm.jsonl page:7: "includes pro forma adjustments for acquisitions and cost savings not reflected in adjusted EBITDA")) but is an analyst inference, not a reported figure, and assumes the term loan and revolver are the first lien debt and cash is fully netted.

Liquidity is cash plus undrawn revolver: 373 + 659 = 1,032 at September 30, 2026 ((10-Q_2026-09-30_apg-20260930.htm.jsonl page:56: "$1,032 million of total liquidity")), down from 912 + 745 = 1,657 at December 31, 2025 and 499 + 494 = 993 at December 31, 2024. No committed facility expires within twelve months: the revolver matures in 2031 and the term loan in 2033 after the Ninth Amendment; the 2029 notes are the first bond maturities. Hedging: (10-Q_2026-09-30_apg-20260930.htm.jsonl page:24: "the 2026 Interest Rate Swap with $720 of notional value, exchanging one-month SOFR for a fixed rate of 3.59% per annum") and a second swap of 400 notional; (10-Q_2026-09-30_apg-20260930.htm.jsonl page:25: "The remaining $1,027 of the term loan balance will bear interest based on one-month SOFR plus 175 basis points"); the 720 forward-starting swap matures in January 2029 ((10-Q_2026-09-30_apg-20260930.htm.jsonl page:25: "commencing in October 2026 and maturing in January 2029")), before the term loan maturity in 2033, so floating exposure on the term loan returns thereafter. Fixed coupons on the three note series total about 56 a year (Calculations). The issuer-reported fair values at September 30, 2026 were 318 for the 4.125% notes, 263 for the 4.750% notes and 473 for the 5.750% notes (carrying values 337, 277 and 500), i.e. all three below carrying value; fair values are issuer estimates from discounting at available rates (Level 2), not traded prices.
### Cash flow and funding

Nine-month 2026 operating cash flow of 393 compares with 377 a year earlier, with working capital absorbing cash ((10-Q_2026-09-30_apg-20260930.htm.jsonl page:4: "Accounts receivable (232) (58)"); (10-Q_2026-09-30_apg-20260930.htm.jsonl page:4: "Contract assets (213) (112)")) partly offset by contract liabilities (+202). Operating cash flow is seasonal: derived Q4 2025 operating cash flow was 382 (759 less 377), which is why nine-month cash conversion looks weaker than FY2025. Free cash flow of 317 for nine months 2026 covered less than a fifth of the combined 1,608 of acquisitions and buybacks (1,356 plus 252); the rest came from (10-Q_2026-09-30_apg-20260930.htm.jsonl page:5: "Proceeds from long-term borrowings 795") (net of (10-Q_2026-09-30_apg-20260930.htm.jsonl page:5: "Payments on long-term borrowings (310)")), (10-Q_2026-09-30_apg-20260930.htm.jsonl page:5: "Net short-term debt 335") and the cash balance. The issuer's adjusted free cash flow was 468 for nine months 2026 against 434 ((EX-99.1_2026-10-29_apg-20260930xexx991.htm.jsonl page:15: "Adjusted free cash flow $ 240 $ 248 $ 468 $ 434")), at 84.2% conversion of adjusted net income against a full-year guide of (EX-99.1_2026-10-29_apg-20260930xexx991.htm.jsonl page:3: "Adjusted free cash flow conversion of 110%"); the guide implies a strong fourth quarter and is a management claim. Subsequent to quarter-end the company borrowed another 100 on the revolver ((10-Q_2026-09-30_apg-20260930.htm.jsonl page:24: "Subsequent to September 30, 2026, the Company borrowed an additional $100 under the Revolving Credit Facility for general corporate purposes")) and repurchased shares for about 143 ((10-Q_2026-09-30_apg-20260930.htm.jsonl page:37: "Subsequent to September 30, 2026, the Company repurchased 3,604,478 shares of common stock for approximately $143 under the 2025 SRP")), with 607 of the authorisation remaining, so post-quarter net debt is higher than the September 30 figure.

Segment earnings are the issuer's adjusted measure (E3 page 13 and Q3 10-Q segment note). Q3 2026 gross margin fell to 30.1% from 31.3% ((EX-99.1_2026-10-29_apg-20260930xexx991.htm.jsonl page:1: "Gross profit margin 30.1 % 31.3 % (120) bps")) on project mix and rising material and fuel costs, while adjusted EBITDA margin rose 20 bps to 13.7%; the quarter's reported revenue growth was 22.5% against organic growth of 15.7%, so 6.8 percentage points of growth (22.5 less 15.7) came from acquisitions and currency. Acquisitions contributed little profit so far: (10-Q_2026-09-30_apg-20260930.htm.jsonl page:10: "net revenues and operating loss from the Company's material acquisitions that closed over the previous twelve months were $183 and $3") for nine months. | Letters of credit posted as insurance collateral | Approximately 153 at Dec 31, 2025; the issuing facility is not identified and only 5 reduced revolver availability; no Sep 30, 2026 figure supplied | No | (10-K_2025-12-31_apg-20251231.htm.jsonl page:95: "The Company has outstanding letters of credit as collateral totaling approximately $153 and $147") |

Definition risks: adjusted EBITDA excludes systems and business enablement costs (82 for nine months 2026, 61 for nine months 2025, 96 for FY2025), acquisition and divestiture costs (39 and 12 for nine months) and non-service pension cost; the reported EBITDA-based leverage is therefore materially higher (3.61x total, 3.23x net, LTM). Cash interest is net of interest income. Leases are excluded from debt and from EBITDA-based leverage. Restricted cash is not deducted. ## Findings
### Reader summary
| Bottom line | Confidence | Main limitation |

| APi Group is a diversified, acquisitive fire, life safety and specialty services company with low customer concentration. In 2026 it spent heavily on acquisitions, funded by a new 500 million note issue, revolver borrowing and cash. | Medium | Recurring revenue share, legal documents and ownership percentages are not supplied, so durability and creditor protections cannot be sized. |
| Finding | Creditor impact | Confidence |

| Work is split between inspection, service and monitoring contracts and project work, and no customer exceeded 5% of net revenues in 2025. | Diversification lowers single-customer risk, but the recurring share of revenue is not disclosed, so revenue durability cannot be quantified. | Medium |

| 2026 acquisitions of CertaSite, Onyx-Fire and WTech were closed for 271, 532 and 394 million, alongside ten smaller deals for 227 million. | Debt-funded growth raised leverage before the acquired earnings are fully in the numbers, so integration success drives the deleveraging path. | High |

| Buybacks and related-party flows continue alongside acquisitions: 252 million of repurchases in nine months, further repurchases after quarter-end, and Series A stock converting at the end of 2026. | Capital returns compete with debt reduction; no creditor-adverse action is documented, but the documents that would show legal capacity are not supplied. | Medium |

| Filings give different totals for 2025 acquisition consideration (233, 235 and 225 million) without explanation. | Purchase accounting and accrued consideration may still be changing, so acquisition spend and contingent liabilities carry some uncertainty. | Medium |
### Business and transaction view

APi Group Corporation is a US-listed holding company whose subsidiaries deliver fire and life safety, security, elevator and escalator, and specialty contracting, fabrication and infrastructure services, reported as two segments, Safety Services and Specialty Services. Safety Services, which is mostly contracted inspection, service and monitoring plus installation, carried FY2025 revenue of 5,456, with Specialty Services at 2,460, and about two thirds of revenue is United States based. The creditor-relevant strengths are documented diversification (no customer above 5% of 2025 net revenues), statutory and insurance-driven inspection demand described by management, a cost base the company describes as largely variable, and capital spending that management puts below 1.5% of net revenues. The weaknesses are equally documented: Specialty Services and part of Safety Services are project-driven, fixed-price contract cost estimation is a critical audit matter, gross margin fell in Q3 2026 on mix and input costs, margins and cash flow are seasonal (net revenues are typically lower in the first and second quarters), and the share of revenue that is truly recurring is not quantified in any supplied source. The decisive change for a creditor is the 2026 acquisition programme: CertaSite (February), Onyx-Fire (June) and WTech (July) closed for a combined 1,197, funded by a 500 million 5.750% senior note issue in May, a larger and extended revolver, revolver draws and a fall in cash, so that last-twelve-months total debt over adjusted EBITDA is 3.02x and net 2.71x (CP-1, derived), against 2.67x and 1.79x at FY2025. Management pairs the acquisitions with continued share repurchases (252 in nine months and about 143 after quarter-end) and a Series A Preferred Stock that converts into 6,000,000 common shares on the last day of 2026. No priming, uptier, drop-down, collateral release or debt-funded dividend recapitalisation is documented in the supplied sources; the 2024 conversion and repurchase of the Series B Preferred Stock was part debt-funded and is the closest precedent for shareholder-return financing. These statements are limited by the absence of the executed financing documents, which would show what the issuer is permitted to do.

### Transaction summary and new debt issues

The transaction set for this snapshot is a series of 2026 acquisitions and the financing around them; there is no single sponsor transaction. In the first quarter of 2026 the company closed CertaSite on February 2 for 271 ((10-Q_2026-09-30_apg-20260930.htm.jsonl page:8: "On February 2, 2026, the Company completed the acquisition of CertaSite, LLC")), an inspection-first fire and life safety provider reported in Safety Services. On April 17 and April 22, 2026 it signed agreements for WTech Fire Group (about €324 in cash) and Onyx-Fire Protection Services (about C$725 in cash, from funds managed by Blackstone Tactical Opportunities) ((10-Q_2026-03-31_apg-20260331.htm.jsonl page:30: "Wtech will be acquired for approximately €324 in cash")). Onyx-Fire closed on June 8, 2026 for 532 ((10-Q_2026-09-30_apg-20260930.htm.jsonl page:8: "On June 8, 2026, the Company completed the acquisition of Onyx-Fire Protection Services, Inc.")) and WTech on July 1, 2026 for about 394 in cash ((10-Q_2026-09-30_apg-20260930.htm.jsonl page:8: "On July 1, 2026, the Company completed the acquisition of WTech Fire Group")); ten further acquisitions in nine months added 227 of consideration. Purchase accounting is provisional for all 2026 acquisitions ((10-Q_2026-09-30_apg-20260930.htm.jsonl page:9: "The Company has not finalized its accounting for any of the acquisitions completed during 2026")), and the filings do not state any relationship between the Blackstone funds that sold Onyx-Fire and the Blackstone entities that held the former Series B Preferred Stock; none is inferred.

New debt issues and amendments: on May 14, 2026 the company's subsidiary APi Group DE issued 500 of 5.750% Senior Notes due June 1, 2034 ((10-Q_2026-09-30_apg-20260930.htm.jsonl page:60: "On May 14, 2026, APi Group DE completed a private offering of $500 million aggregate principal amount of 5.750% Senior Notes due 2034")), guaranteed on a senior unsecured basis by the parent and certain subsidiaries, with proceeds for general corporate purposes including previously announced acquisitions; in Q2 2026 the Ninth Amendment raised the revolver commitment from 750 to 1,000, extended the revolver to May 14, 2031 and extended the 2021 Term Loan to May 14, 2033 ((10-Q_2026-09-30_apg-20260930.htm.jsonl page:24: "extended the maturity date of the 2021 Term Loan to May 14, 2033")). Subsequent events (after September 30, 2026, before the cutoff): a further 100 revolver borrowing for general corporate purposes and repurchases of about 143 of shares, leaving 607 of the repurchase authorisation ((10-Q_2026-09-30_apg-20260930.htm.jsonl page:24: "Subsequent to September 30, 2026, the Company borrowed an additional $100 under the Revolving Credit Facility for general corporate purposes")). The liquidity effect is set out in the CP-1 handoff (1,032 of liquidity at September 30, 2026; 559 of revolver availability at October 29, 2026). Preceding history that shapes the capital structure: in 2024 the company converted the Series B Preferred Stock into common stock and immediately repurchased half of the conversion shares for 600, financed by an incremental 300 term facility and cash ((10-K_2025-12-31_apg-20251231.htm.jsonl page:74: "an incremental term facility of $300 million and (ii) cash and available credit from the balance sheet")), and issued 18,975,000 common shares to help fund the Elevated acquisition. A future contract term, not an event: the Series A Preferred Stock converts into 6,000,000 common shares on the last day of 2026 ((10-Q_2026-09-30_apg-20260930.htm.jsonl page:29: "will be convertible into 6,000,000 shares of common stock upon conversion on the last day of 2026")), with an annual dividend payable in shares or cash at the company's sole option, which management intends to settle in shares ((10-K_2025-12-31_apg-20251231.htm.jsonl page:57: "We intend to settle these dividends in shares of Common Stock")). The pack contains no purchase agreements, indentures, credit agreement or amendment, so use of proceeds and permitted-payment capacity rest on filing summaries.
### Ownership, governance and sponsor behaviour
Assessment is of issuer-level, documented actions only; no inference is drawn from the identity of any holder, and no individual is assessed.
| Behaviour category | Documented action | Legal capacity, willingness, feasibility | Evidence quality | Scoring dimension |

| Neutral or Mixed | 2024 Series B conversion with a 600 repurchase of half the conversion shares, part debt-funded; 2025 and 2026 buybacks under a 1,000 authorisation (252 in nine months 2026 and about 143 after quarter-end) while revolver borrowing rose | Capacity: Credit Agreement restricts distributions in customary terms per the MD&A summary but baskets are not supplied (Insufficient Information). Willingness: repeated repurchases documented. Feasibility: liquidity of 1,032 and covenant ratio of 1.6:1.0 (CP-1) | High for the actions ((10-K_2025-12-31_apg-20251231.htm.jsonl page:74: "we agreed to immediately repurchase one-half of the Conversion Shares")); Low for capacity | Capital allocation; sponsor alignment |

spans.text: ## Request

This is the fundamental credit synthesis for APi Group Corp (APG, issuer id apg) as of 2026-11-05, on the credit_snapshot pathway, current period Q3 2026 against FY2025, in USD. It combines the financial base from the CP-1 handoff with the business and transaction context from the CP-1A handoff and reads no filing text directly.
## Sources
### Issuer sources underlying the upstream handoffs
This module quotes no source text; every fact comes from the upstream handoffs below, which relied on these pinned sources.
| Source (exact name) | sha256 |
### Handoffs supplied
| Module | sha256 | Use |
| CP-0 | d40ba3564c8793d91987b4dca76c3187df72cdc74c99584f6e488aad8f306a91 | Source limits and source differences |
| CP-1 | f7db30806e7a98570fba7e4bc97f39d6f69658956a05590382766f0c4cdbcca8 | Financial base, leverage, liquidity, covenant position |
| CP-1A | 49e3ff078b6908f3efb88a445708e93fc6e79232aec6b0d708d47eaa20df5368 | Business model, transaction set, governance behaviour, conflicts |
The run context (sha256 5361f531841cad8936701ac126679da0830e0b3a545fa6b1b9ab2f313f6dfc9d) holds dated settings only and is not issuer evidence.
## Findings
### Reader summary
| Bottom line | Confidence | Main limitation |

| APi Group is a diversified, cash-generative services business whose leverage rose in 2026 as acquisitions and buybacks were debt-funded: total debt over adjusted EBITDA is 3.02x on a last-twelve-months basis against 2.67x at FY2025. | Medium | Executed financing documents are not supplied, so covenant definitions, guarantors and permitted payments cannot be verified. |
| Finding | Creditor impact | Confidence |

| Net debt over adjusted EBITDA rose to 2.71x from 1.79x as acquisitions of USD 1,356 million and buybacks of USD 252 million were funded with debt and cash. | The balance sheet has less room for earnings shocks, and deleveraging now depends on integration and restraint in shareholder returns. | High |

| Liquidity is USD 1,032 million at September 30, 2026, and no bond or committed facility matures before 2029 apart from small short-term loans. | Near-term refinancing risk is low, but liquidity is USD 625 million lower than at FY2025. | High |

| Revolver usage was 33.5% at September 30, 2026, above the 30% trigger of the springing first lien test reported at 1.6:1.0 against 3.75 to 1.00. | Reported headroom is wide, but the test applies and its EBITDA definition cannot be checked. | Medium |

| Customers are diversified and demand is regulation-driven, but the recurring share of revenue is not disclosed. | Revenue durability supports debt service qualitatively but cannot be sized. | Medium |
### Credit view

APi Group Corp is a sound, cash-generative services business whose credit profile weakened in 2026 because acquisitions and buybacks were funded with debt. Its strongest support is diversified, regulation-driven demand, with no customer above 5% of FY2025 net revenues, adjusted EBITDA of USD 896 million for nine months 2026, and debt maturities that start in 2029 apart from small short-term loans. The weakest point is balance sheet capacity: last-twelve-months total debt over adjusted EBITDA is 3.02x (net 2.71x) against 2.67x (1.79x) at FY2025, liquidity is USD 1,032 million, and revolver usage is above the springing-covenant trigger. Whether the rise proves temporary depends on integrating the USD 1,197 million of named 2026 acquisitions and on restraint in buybacks; unverified covenant definitions limit confidence.
### Key findings

First, leverage stepped up sharply in nine months 2026 (Analyst Interpretation on CP-1 figures). Total debt obligations rose to USD 3,601 million from USD 2,776 million at FY2025 and cash fell to USD 373 million from USD 912 million, so net debt rose by USD 1,364 million [CP-1, leverage and Calculations]. The mechanism is that acquisition spend of USD 1,356 million (net of cash acquired; named deals CertaSite, Onyx-Fire and WTech cost USD 1,197 million combined) and buybacks of USD 252 million exceeded free cash flow of USD 317 million, and the acquired EBITDA enters the trailing figure only from closing dates, so reported leverage overstates run-rate leverage while also resting on unproven integration [CP-1; CP-1A, transaction summary]. The implication is a lower cushion against a margin or volume shock until earnings catch up, with last-twelve-months cash interest cover of 9.23x flattering the position because the USD 500 million 5.750% notes issued in May 2026 and the revolver draw have only partly reached cash interest; Q3 2026 interest expense, net, was USD 45 million against USD 34 million a year earlier, and an annualised Q3 figure gives about 6.62x (indicative, CP-1) (Analyst Interpretation).

Second, liquidity is adequate but thinner (Documentary Fact on CP-1 figures). Liquidity was USD 1,032 million at September 30, 2026 (USD 373 million cash and USD 659 million undrawn revolver), against USD 1,657 million at FY2025, and revolver availability was USD 559 million at October 29, 2026 after a further USD 100 million draw, a subsequent event. The revolver matures in 2031 and the term loan in 2033 after the Ninth Amendment, and the notes mature in 2029 and 2034, so there is no near-term wall; the implication is that debt service and refinancing risk are manageable, but the revolver is now the funding buffer for seasonal cash flow, with operating cash flow back-end loaded.

Third, the only maintenance covenant is a springing first lien net leverage test that applies at the latest quarter-end (Documentary Fact for the reported ratio, Analyst Interpretation for the trigger). Revolver usage of 33.5% exceeded the 30% trigger at September 30, 2026, and the reported ratio of 1.6:1.0 compares with a 3.75 to 1.00 limit, 2.15x of headroom on rounded figures [CP-1, covenant position]. The credit agreement is not supplied, so the covenant EBITDA definition is unverified; CP-1's indicative implied covenant EBITDA of about USD 1,318 million against derived last-twelve-months adjusted EBITDA of USD 1,191 million depends on pro forma adjustments the issuer describes but the pack does not quantify. The implication is that headroom looks wide on reported terms but is not independently verified.

Fourth, earnings are growing but cash conversion lags and margins are under input-cost pressure (Documentary Fact). Adjusted EBITDA was USD 896 million for nine months 2026 against USD 746 million, while operating cash flow was USD 393 million against USD 377 million as receivables and contract assets absorbed cash and Q3 2026 gross margin fell to 30.1% from 31.3% on project mix and material and fuel costs [CP-1]. Fixed-price contract cost estimation is a critical audit matter and cost overruns hit margin directly [CP-1A, operating model], so the implication is that growth is not yet translating into proportionate free cash flow, though the fourth quarter is seasonally strong (derived fourth quarter 2025 operating cash flow of USD 382 million).

Fifth, capital allocation is shareholder-friendly alongside leverage build (Analyst Interpretation). Repurchases of USD 252 million in nine months 2026 and about USD 143 million after quarter-end sat beside revolver borrowing; the 2024 Series B conversion and USD 600 million repurchase was part debt-funded [CP-1A, governance]. No priming, uptier, drop-down or debt-funded dividend recapitalisation is documented, but the executed documents showing legal capacity are not supplied, so the implication is a Neutral or Mixed behaviour assessment with legal capacity unassessed.

Sixth, the evidence has known limits (Documentary Fact). Filings give different totals for 2025 acquisition consideration (USD 233 million, USD 235 million and USD 225 million) [CP-1A, conflicts], the issuer of record of the notes differs between the MD&A and the exhibit index [CP-0], and the recurring revenue share and ownership concentration are not disclosed [CP-1A]. The implication is that revenue durability and creditor protections are described qualitatively only.
### Strengths and weaknesses

Strengths. (1) Customer diversification and regulation-driven demand: no customer above 5% of FY2025 net revenues, statutory and insurance-driven inspection demand per management (Documentary Fact for the concentration, Management Language for the demand characterisation) [CP-1A, company profile]; the mechanism is lower single-name revenue risk and less discretionary service demand, implying steadier cash flow than a pure project contractor. (2) Earnings momentum: adjusted EBITDA of USD 896 million for nine months 2026 against USD 746 million, with revenue up in both segments (Documentary Fact) [CP-1]; implying capacity to absorb the acquisition debt if growth persists. (3) Debt structure and market access: maturities begin in 2029 with fixed-rate notes, an extended revolver (2031) and term loan (2033), and a USD 500 million note issue completed in May 2026 (Documentary Fact) [CP-1; CP-1A]; implying low refinancing pressure and demonstrated market access. (4) Low capital intensity: free cash flow after capex of USD 317 million in nine months 2026 and capex management puts below 1.5% of net revenues (Documentary Fact for the cash figure, Management Language for the claim) [CP-1; CP-1A]; implying the business converts EBITDA to cash outside working capital swings. (5) Wide reported covenant headroom of 2.15x (Documentary Fact, unverified definitions) [CP-1].

Weaknesses. (1) Higher leverage from debt-funded acquisitions: 3.02x total and 2.71x net on last-twelve-months adjusted EBITDA (Documentary Fact on derived CP-1 figures); the mechanism is purchase prices in debt before acquired earnings fully arrive, implying thinner cushion and dependence on integration. Reported (unadjusted) EBITDA gives 3.61x and 3.23x, and the add-backs are material, so the choice of EBITDA measure matters (CP-1). (2) Capital returns alongside leverage build: USD 252 million of buybacks plus about USD 143 million after quarter-end (Documentary Fact); implying deleveraging relies on earnings growth rather than debt paydown. (3) Springing covenant trigger exceeded and definitions unverified (Documentary Fact for usage, Insufficient Information for the covenant mechanics). (4) Revenue durability unquantified and project exposure: the recurring share is not disclosed, contracts are mostly under six months, fixed-price estimation is a critical audit matter and Q3 2026 gross margin fell (Documentary Fact; Insufficient Information for the recurring share) [CP-1A]; implying margin and cash volatility that cannot be sized. (5) Rising and partly floating interest cost: the term loan floats on SOFR with hedges that end before its 2033 maturity (the forward swap matures in January 2029), and the new notes carry a 5.750% coupon (Documentary Fact) [CP-1]; implying higher interest burden after the swaps roll off. (6) Documentation gaps: no credit agreement, indentures or guarantor list, and unresolved issuer of record for the notes (Insufficient Information) [CP-0; CP-1A].
### Fundamental credit assessment and thesis
| Element | Statement | Category | Confidence | Basis |

| Assessment | The business is solid and diversified with adequate liquidity and no near-term maturity wall, but 2026 debt-funded acquisitions and buybacks have raised leverage and made the covenant position and run-rate earnings dependent on integration and unverified definitions | Analyst Interpretation | Medium | CP-1 leverage, liquidity, covenant; CP-1A operating model, transaction summary, governance |

| Thesis | Cash-generative, diversified services earnings support debt service, but the credit depends on whether 2026 acquisitions deliver the earnings that bring leverage back down while buybacks continue | Analyst Interpretation | Medium | CP-1 and CP-1A as above |

Confidence is below High because the readiness handoff recorded READY_WITH_LIMITATIONS, the business handoff records the recurring-share and ownership gaps, and no executed financing documents are supplied.
### Key credit risks
| Risk | Mechanic | Credit implication | Severity |

| Integration and leverage | Debt-funded USD 1,197 million of named acquisitions with earnings only partly in the trailing figures | Leverage stays elevated if integration lags; deleveraging relies on EBITDA growth | Material |
| Capital allocation | Buybacks and revolver draws in the same period as the leverage rise | Cushion erodes if returns continue before leverage falls | Material |
| Covenant trigger and documentation | Springing test applies with revolver usage above 30%; definitions and baskets not supplied | Headroom and permitted-payment capacity unverified | Material |
| Margin and cost estimation | Fixed-price work, input-cost pressure and Q3 2026 gross margin decline | Earnings and cash flow volatility not quantifiable | Material |
| Interest cost | New 5.750% notes, revolver borrowing and floating term loan after hedge expiry | Cash interest cover likely lower than the trailing 9.23x | Material |
| Seasonality and working capital | Revenue lower in the first and second quarters; receivables and contract assets absorbed cash | Revolver is the buffer for intra-year swings | Minor |
## Calculations
All inputs are printed in the upstream handoffs; USD millions.
| Calculation | Inputs | Result |
| Liquidity change, FY2025 to September 30, 2026 | 1,657 - 1,032 | USD 625 million lower |
| Net debt change | 3,228 - 1,864 | USD 1,364 million higher |
| Adjusted EBITDA growth, nine months 2026 against 2025 | 896 / 746 - 1 | 20.1% |
| Net revenue growth, nine months 2026 against 2025 | 6,790 / 5,794 - 1 | 17.2% |
| Named 2026 acquisitions | 271 + 532 + 394 | 1,197 |
No other new calculation; leverage, cover, liquidity and covenant figures are taken from the CP-1 handoff as stated there.
## Gaps
| Gap | Why it matters and what it affects | Severity | Action |

| Credit Agreement, Ninth Amendment, indentures, guarantor list: Not supplied | Covenant definitions, baskets, security and note issuer roles unverified; affects covenant headroom and distribution capacity | High | Obtain executed documents |
| Recurring (inspection, service and monitoring) revenue share: Not supplied | Revenue durability cannot be sized | Medium | Request revenue by service type |
| Beneficial ownership and control: Not supplied | Alignment and sponsor-type behaviour cannot be assessed | Medium | Add proxy statement |
| Pro forma acquired EBITDA and run-rate interest: Not supplied | Leverage and cover are overstated and flattered respectively on trailing figures | Medium | Management pro forma and swap schedule |
| 2025 acquisition consideration totals differ by filing: unresolved | Accrued consideration uncertainty | Minor | Cite by filing and period |
| Ratings and market data: Not supplied | No external credit or market view | Minor | Add if required |

| Limitations inherited: readiness handoff READY_WITH_LIMITATIONS and the CP-1A readiness judgment of this module READY_WITH_LIMITATIONS | Confidence capped below High | Not applicable | Carry forward |
## Next module

CP-5 should test that the claims here agree with the CP-1 and CP-1A evidence, in particular the leverage and liquidity figures, the covenant-trigger statement (revolver usage of 33.5% against a 30% trigger) and the acquisition totals, and should record the 2025 acquisition consideration difference as an open conflict. Relative value, security selection and the committee's action bias are outside this module and belong to later modules.
